title: Someone grabs your toy
situation: You were playing nicely, and someone suddenly takes the toy from your hand.
wisdomMove: Say, "Let's take turns," and ask calmly.
explanation: The strong move is not always the loud move. Dharma means doing the right thing even when you feel upset.
valueLine: Wisdom move: protect fairness without losing your calm.

title: A friend tells a lie
situation: Your friend says something untrue, and everyone is looking at you.
wisdomMove: Tell the truth calmly and kindly.
explanation: Satya means truth. Truth becomes more powerful when we speak it with care, not anger.
valueLine: Wisdom move: be honest without trying to hurt someone.

title: You lose a game
situation: Your team loses, and you feel disappointed.
explanation: Dhairya means courage and patience. A brave person can lose, learn, and try again.
valueLine: Wisdom move: use defeat as practice for the next round.

title: Someone is sitting alone
situation: At lunch or class, you notice one child has no one to talk to.
powerMove: Ignore them and stay with your group.
explanation: Seva means service. Small acts of kindness can make someone feel seen and welcome.
valueLine: Wisdom move: include others when you have the chance.

title: You feel very angry
situation: Something unfair happens, and angry words are ready to jump out.
powerMove: React fast and say the first thing.
explanation: Shanti means peace. Pausing gives your mind time to choose the better action.
valueLine: Wisdom move: calm first, words second.

title: You see a mess
situation: After an activity, paper and pencils are scattered around the room.
powerMove: Say, "Not my mess," and walk away.
wisdomMove: Pick up a few things and ask others to help.
explanation: A helpful person does not wait for praise. Seva makes the shared space better for everyone.
valueLine: Wisdom move: start with one useful action.

title: A smaller child makes a mistake
situation: A younger child spills water and looks worried.
powerMove: Laugh and call everyone to see.
wisdomMove: Help clean it and say, "It happens."
explanation: Daya means compassion. Real strength helps people feel safe after a mistake.
valueLine: Wisdom move: correct the problem without shaming the person.

title: You can copy homework
situation: You forgot one answer, and a friend offers to show you theirs.
powerMove: Copy it so you look smart.
wisdomMove: Try your best and ask for help after class.
explanation: Satya also means being honest with yourself. Copying may feel easy, but learning makes you stronger.
valueLine: Wisdom move: choose learning over looking perfect.

title: Two friends are arguing
situation: Both friends want you to take their side immediately.
wisdomMove: Listen to both and help them calm down.
explanation: Viveka means discernment. It helps us pause, listen, and choose what is fair.

title: You win first place
situation: You did very well, and everyone is clapping.
powerMove: Say, "I am better than all of you."
wisdomMove: Thank your team, teacher, and practice.
explanation: Vinaya means humility. A humble winner can celebrate without making others feel small.
valueLine: Wisdom move: enjoy success with gratitude.
